name: $I = \frac{E}{R + r}$
e: Electromotive Force (emf) is written I = (E)/(R + r). Emf is energy per coulomb that a source pumps around a complete loop.

name: $I = \frac{E_1 + E_2}{R + r_1 + r_2}$
e: Batteries in series aiding is written I = (E1 + E2)/(R + r1 + r2). A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add.

name: $I = \frac{E_1 - E_2}{R + r_1 + r_2}$
e: Batteries in series opposing (E1 > E2) is written I = (E1 - E2)/(R + r1 + r2). A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. In series, the same current runs through each part and the voltages add.

name: $I = \frac{E}{R + \frac{r}{2}}$
e: Batteries in parallel is written I = (E)/(R + (r)/(2)). A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. In parallel, the same voltage sits across each branch and the currents add.

name: $W = VIt = I^2Rt = \frac{V^2}{R}t$
e: Electrical energy is written W = VIt = I^2Rt = (V^2)/(R)t. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

name: $P = VI = I^2R = \frac{V^2}{R}$
e: Electrical power is written P = VI = I^2R = (V^2)/(R). Electrical power is the energy transfer rate, P = VI, also I^2R or V^2/R.

name: $W = JH$
content: Joule's law of electricity and heat (Work-Heat relation)
e: Joule's law of electricity and heat (Work-Heat relation) is written W = JH. Joule heat is I^2 R t; it grows with current squared.

name: $H = \frac{I^2Rt}{J}$
e: Heat produced by electric current is written H = (I^2Rt)/(J). Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path.
